fichas.title: Geometrical relationships: triangles and quadrature
fichas.summary: Geometric triangle constructions illustrate quadrature and dimensional relationships. A right-angled isosceles triangle with a baseline-to-height ratio of 2:1 can be used to construct a square of equal area to a given shape. The page also describes a triangle with base and height forming two sides of a square, and the more pointed π/4 triangle attributed to A. v. Drach.
uses: Constructing a square of equal area to a given shape (quadrature)
Establishing dimensional relationships in cathedral design

fichas.title: Octagonal relationships and the 1:√2 rectangle
fichas.summary: The page describes octagonal geometrical relationships based on a diagonal triangle whose height is the diagonal of a square constructed over half its base. The resulting rectangle has a 1:√2 side ratio, retained when the rectangle is halved or doubled. This relationship is cited as the basis for ISO A-series paper formats, with geometric progressions shown through octagon hierarchies.
uses: Deriving proportional rectangles by halving or doubling
Basis for ISO A-series paper formats

dimensions.label: Rectangle side ratio
dimensions.context: The rectangle formed from the diagonal triangle has sides in the ratio 1:√2; halving or doubling preserves the ratio.

fichas.title: Square-root relationships and approximate coordination
fichas.summary: Square-root hierarchies and continued-fraction approximations are presented as tools for coordinating non-rectangular building elements. The page connects approximate square-number values to the MERO space frame, whose screw connections at the nodes compensate for imprecision in right angles. Examples include coordination based on √2 and √3.
uses: Approximating square roots for construction layouts
Developing MERO space frames using approximate square-number values
